definition: Layer normalization is a technique that normalizes the inputs across the features instead of the batch in neural networks.
details: Layer normalization is a technique that normalizes the inputs across the features instead of the batch in neural networks. It is particularly useful in recurrent neural networks.

explainer.lead: Layer normalization stabilizes training by rescaling activations within each example rather than across a batch. That makes it useful when batches are small or sequences vary in length.

tiers.eli5: Like adjusting the volume on each song individually so every track plays at a comfortable level, rather than setting one volume for the whole playlist.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers place it inside recurrent and transformer blocks to keep activations well scaled; a pitfall is misplacing it relative to residual connections, which can hurt convergence.
tiers.paperLevel: Inputs are normalized across the features of a single example, typically recentered and rescaled by learned parameters; it does not depend on batch statistics.

explainer.example: In a sequence model, each time step's feature vector is normalized using its own mean and variance before entering the next operation.
